page: Microsoft Azure F48as_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs with 1 thread per core. The memory configuration totals 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.0 GB per core. Per-core CPU cache allocations include 32 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local ephemeral storage, requiring remote storage solutions.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded compute efficiency. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieved a top-tier stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 147,728.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,839.0. Clang software compilation reached 64,173.0, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 628.62 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Memory subsystem bandwidth registers at 230.45 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 135.74 GB/sec for uncached writes. Single-core performance remains strong, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,101.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3,080.27.

The absence of simultaneous multithreading (SMT) with 1 thread per physical core minimizes resource contention, providing deterministic compute execution across all 48 cores. However, the lack of bundled local storage means applications reliant on local scratch disk access must leverage remote Azure storage volumes. Cost efficiency is driven by high per-core execution density and dedicated hardware mapping rather than shared execution queues.

Microsoft Azure F48as_v6 is suited for parallel compute tasks including software build pipelines, high-throughput batch encoding, continuous integration, CPU-based machine learning inference, and in-memory key-value caching workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F48as_v6 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. With dedicated physical cores mapped one-to-one with its 48 vCPUs, it eliminates thread contention for intensive tasks. The system features 192.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core) and provides support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16. It contains no onboard local storage or GPUs, relying on attached network storage. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-core performance, achieving 147,728.85 in stress-ng and 64,173.0 in Geekbench Clang compilation. Memory bandwidth reaches 230.45 GB/sec for large-block read operations. Given its heavy compute throughput and solid memory capacity, this configuration is well-tailored for code compilation, batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, and high-concurrency microservices.
